requirement:
In authored chapters, requirements, examples, and named definitions render as
collapsible sections, expanded when the chapter opens. Their headers and body
prose share the left edge of the containing prose. Each header identifies the
declaration and its kind. A light vertical rule on the right delineates the
section; a circular disclosure control at the top of that rule shows a minus
when expanded and a plus when collapsed. Collapsing a section hides its body
while keeping the header visible. The disclosure works with a mouse or keyboard.

The body retains its Markdown rendering, including code blocks and nested
declarations. Requirement and example headers retain the definition and
evidence links described by {cite}`requirements.index.navigation`; those
links navigate independently of the disclosure.
rationale:
The tests adequately check `requirements.index.declaration_sections`. I found no gap.

**Structure and rendering** (`src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[declaration_sections_contain_their_headers_and_markdown_bodies]`). The test runs `preprocess_book` on a chapter and renders the result to HTML.
- **Collapsible and open by default.** A requirement, a nested example and a named definition each become `<details class="habeas-declaration" open>`. The test asserts exactly 3 `open` details, 3 `</details>`, 3 `<summary>` and 3 `</summary>`.
- **Header identifies kind.** The requirement and example headers carry `alt="req rules.ready"` and `alt="example rules.case"`. The definition header carries the `habeas-definition-label` span reading "definition" and its phrase "alpha & beta".
- **Header and body are separate.** The header text, taken up to `</summary>`, must not contain `habeas-declaration-body`. The body sits in `<div class="habeas-declaration-body">`, so collapsing hides the body and keeps the header.
- **Markdown body and nesting.** The test asserts that bold and emphasis render, that the fenced Rust code block renders as `language-rust`, and that the nested example sits inside the requirement body. It also asserts the trailing prose "The requirement ends here." stays inside the outer body.
- **Header links.** For both the requirement and the example, the header contains the `#habeas-{kind}-rules.{name}` anchor link and the `requirements-index/rules.{name}.html` evidence link. Both links therefore sit inside the summary, outside the body.
- **Surrounding prose.** "Before." and "After." render outside the sections.

**Styling** (`src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[declaration_styles_distinguish_disclosure_state_and_keyboard_focus]`). This test parses the stylesheet and checks these rules:
- **Right rule.** `.habeas-declaration` has a `border-right` and `padding-right`.
- **Left edge.** `.habeas-declaration` has a zero left margin (`margin: 1.25em 0.8em 1.25em 0`), and `.habeas-declaration-body` has `padding: 0`. I confirmed in `md/habeas.css` that the section has no left padding.
- **Circular control.** `.habeas-declaration > summary::after` has `content: "+"`, `position: absolute`, `top: 0`, `right: -0.7em` and `border-radius: 50%`.
- **Expanded state.** `.habeas-declaration[open] > summary::after` has `content: "−"`.
- **Keyboard.** `summary:focus-visible::after` has an outline. The keyboard obligation rests on the native `details`/`summary` element, which the structure test confirms is used.
- **Badge in header.** The badge keeps `overflow-x: auto` within the summary.

**Supporting test** (`colon_directives_render_markdown_bodies_and_legacy_roles_stay_literal`). It checks that a colon-fenced directive body keeps its Markdown, including a heading and a code fence, and that the fence line itself is removed.

**Links in the header.** The header-link obligation points to `requirements.index.navigation`, which is cited here, not subject to reassessment. The tests still check that those links sit in the header.

All obligations in the subject text map to concrete assertions: collapsible and open by default, kind identification, right rule, circular plus/minus control, hidden body with visible header, keyboard focus, retained Markdown, nested declarations, and header links. Mouse and keyboard operation relies on the native `details` element, so there is no conditional behavior of our own to test beyond the focus style.

text: In authored chapters, requirements, examples, and named definitions render as
collapsible sections, expanded when the chapter opens. Their headers and body
prose share the left edge of the containing prose. Each header identifies the
declaration and its kind. A light vertical rule on the right delineates the
section; a circular disclosure control at the top of that rule shows a minus
when expanded and a plus when collapsed. Collapsing a section hides its body
while keeping the header visible. The disclosure works with a mouse or keyboard.
The body retains its Markdown rendering, including code blocks and nested
declarations. Requirement and example headers retain the definition and
links navigate independently of the disclosure.

Each requirement and example definition badge MUST link to its own anchored definition on the current page. The badge MUST have a separate adjacent link containing an accessible right-arrow icon in an integrated segment matching the badge color linking to its evidence detail page. The badge and arrow MUST remain aligned in one non-wrapping row. Definitions MUST NOT be followed by a separate plaintext evidence link. Each detail page MUST link back to the definition's anchored badge and to the index. Reference badges MUST continue to link to the definition. These links MUST resolve when a requirement name contains `.md`, as in `requirements.cli.mdbook`.
